patterns.usage_note: The emphatic, conversational stretching of ばかり, and it usually carries the speaker's exasperation at someone stuck on one thing. After a noun it means the person does or has nothing but that (ゲームばっかり); after a dictionary-form verb it means they do nothing except that action, typically running on into 〜ばかりで. Keep it apart from 〜たばかり "has just done", a different construction entirely; and note that speech leans even harder on 〜てばかりいる, which this corpus rule does not license.

examples.ruby: 息子[むすこ]は休[やす]みの日[ひ]はゲームばっかりしている。
examples.english: My son does nothing but play video games on his days off.

examples.ruby: あの人[ひと]は文句[もんく]ばっかりで、手[て]を動[うご]かさない。
examples.english: All that guy does is complain; he never lifts a finger.

examples.ruby: 妹[いもうと]は泣[な]くばっかりで、何[なに]があったか話[はな]さない。
examples.english: My sister just cries and won't tell me what happened.
